one_line: Akbar’s finance minister who systematized Mughal land revenue with the dahsala reforms.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s to early 50s, medium height, lean but sturdy build, with the calm bearing of a seasoned administrator.
appearance.face: Oval face with a high forehead, wheatish complexion, neatly trimmed black beard with light grey at the chin, sharp nose, thoughtful dark eyes under slightly arched brows; default expression is composed and analytical, often with a faint, knowing half-smile.
appearance.hair: Hair kept short and neat under a deep maroon Mughal-style turban (pagri) wrapped low and firm, with a thin gold band at the base and a small, single white feather tucked on the left side.
appearance.costume: A long, knee-length Mughal angarkha of fine off‑white cotton with a subtle vertical stripe weave, overlapping right panel tied with thin inner cords; over it a sleeveless, hip-length dark indigo quilted waistcoat (nimcha) with simple diamond stitching and narrow gold piping at the edges; a broad, soft belt (patka) of muted saffron silk with a fine green border wraps twice around his waist, knotted to the left hip with the tasselled ends hanging; loose, straight churidar trousers in light beige taper neatly at the ankles; on his feet, brown leather mojari shoes with modest turned-up toes; minimal jewellery: a single string of small tulsi-like beads at the neck and a plain gold ring on his right hand, projecting dignity without ostentation.
appearance.signature: A long bamboo measuring rod (jarib) marked with dark ink divisions, carried in his left hand or slung across his shoulder with a simple cotton cord, often accompanied by a rolled palm-leaf or paper ledger tucked into his sash.

ref_desc: Raja Todar Mal is a late‑middle‑aged, wheatish‑complexioned man with an oval face, short hair under a maroon turban with a white feather, off‑white angarkha, dark indigo quilted waistcoat, saffron patka, beige churidar, brown mojari shoes, and a bamboo jarib measuring rod with a tucked ledger.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Raja Todar Mal: a late-40s to early-50s, medium-height, lean but sturdy man with an oval face, wheatish complexion, high forehead, neatly trimmed black beard greying at the chin, sharp nose, and thoughtful dark eyes with a calm, analytical expression and faint half-smile. His short hair is covered by a deep maroon Mughal turban wrapped low and firm, ringed by a thin gold band at the base with a single small white feather tucked on the left. He wears a knee-length off‑white cotton angarkha with a subtle vertical stripe texture, its right panel overlapping and tied, over which sits a hip-length dark indigo quilted sleeveless waistcoat with simple diamond stitching and narrow gold piping. Around his waist is a broad muted saffron silk patka with a fine green border, wrapped twice and knotted at his left hip, tasselled ends hanging. His trousers are light beige churidar narrowing neatly at the ankles, and he wears brown leather mojari shoes with modest upturned toes. Keep jewellery minimal: a single string of small beads at his neck and a plain gold ring on his right hand. His signature prop is a long bamboo measuring rod marked with dark divisions, held in his left hand or resting along his shoulder, with a small rolled ledger tucked securely into his waist sash. Show him from multiple angles to fix the face, turban, layered garments, and colours, emphasizing dignified, historically grounded Mughal official attire with an analytical, composed presence.
